name: Grassroots Grants

funder.name: Landscape Board Hills and Fleurieu (South Australia)

summary: Annual small grants for community groups, volunteers and landholders in the Adelaide Hills and Fleurieu to restore land, water and nature, such as revegetation, creek protection and bushcare, with a required co-contribution.

geography.label: Adelaide Hills and Fleurieu, South Australia

amount.note: Two tiers: under $5,000 and up to $20,000

eligibility.rule: Is a legal entity, or applies through an eligible sponsor
If a commercial business applies, its project and activities must be not-for-profit
Not house or garden landscaping or amenity work, and not a community or edible garden
Schools must apply for a dedicated environmental project, not regular activities

documents: Sponsor's letter, if using a sponsor

applicant_types.quote: An applicant must be a 'legal entity', such as: Individuals

geography.quote: Grants are available for projects across the Adelaide Hills and Fleurieu

access.quote: Grassroots Grants open for applications each year in February or March and typically remain open for six weeks.

window.quote: Grassroots Grants open for applications each year in February or March and typically remain open for six weeks.

amount.quote: in two funding tiers: less than $5,000 and up to $20,000

co_finance_required.quote: Our Grassroots Grants require a 50% co-contribution, this means for every $1 of grant funding requested, there must be at least 50 cents of other contributions.

eligibility.quote: Applicants who are not a legal entity will need to seek an eligible sponsor.
I run a commercial business, can I apply? Yes, as long as the project and activities are not-for-profit

Funding will not be provided for projects such as general house and garden landscaping/amenity activities for private homes, sporting clubs, schools and early learning centres. Community gardens including edible gardens will also not be considered.
Schools must demonstrate that they are applying for a dedicated environmental project, not for regular school activities such as general grounds-keeping.

co_finance.quote: time and effort from you or volunteers (valued at $50.50 per hour), also called in-kind contributions. Our Grassroots Grants require a 50% co-contribution, this means for every $1 of grant funding requested, there must be at least 50 cents of other contributions.

after_award.quote: If you are not a legal entity e.g. a group of neighbouring landholders working together for pest management activities, you will need a person or organisation to be responsible for receiving and managing grant funding and reporting.

documents.quote: A sponsor's letter is required to be submitted with your application if you are using a sponsor.
